Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference number: POC-17B712A980-60478
Member: Emerson Delgado
Member ID: W775387988
Requested service: Rotator cuff repair, CPT 29827
Date of denial notice: 2026-08-06
Appeal deadline: 2027-02-02

To the PacificSource Appeal and Grievance Department:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for rotator cuff repair (CPT 29827), as stated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-06, reference number POC-17B712A980-60478. The stated reason for denial was that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity."

I understand that PacificSource applies Medical Policy Manual, Surgery, Policy No. 228, "Shoulder Surgeries" (SUR228), to determine medical necessity for rotator cuff repair. That policy states, in relevant part:

"I. Rotator cuff repair may be considered medically necessary when all of the following Criteria are met (A.-D.): A. Documentation of function-limiting pain (e.g., loss of shoulder function which interferes with the ability to carry out activities of daily living and/or demands of employment); and B. Either of the following criteria are met: 1. Failure to respond to at least three months of non-surgical management which includes documentation of physical therapy or prescribed home exercise program and one or more of the following unless contraindicated: a. Trial of anti-inflammatory medication; or b. Cortisone injection; or 2. The individual suffers from a discrete traumatic event that results in an acute full-thickness rotator cuff tear and has associated function limiting pain; and"

"C. Individual meets all of the following Criteria (1. and 2.) on physical examination when compared to the non-involved side: 1. Either of the following: a. Functionally limited active range of motion; or b. Measurable loss of strength of the rotator cuff musculature; and 2. One or more of the following positive orthopedic tests/signs: a. Drop Arm Test; or b. Painful Arc Test; or c. Jobe or Empty Can Test; or d. External Rotation Lag Sign (Dropping Sign); or e. Internal Rotation Lag Sign; or f. Lift-Off Test; or g. Bear Hug Test; or h. Belly-Press Test (Napoleon); or i. Belly-Off Test; or j. Neer Impingement Test; or k. Hawkins-Kennedy Impingement; or l. Hornblower Test (Patte); and"

"D. Advanced diagnostic imaging study (e.g., MRI, CT) demonstrates a partial-thickness rotator cuff tear or a full-thickness rotator cuff tear that correlates with the individual's reported symptoms and physical exam findings."

My clinical record demonstrates that all four criteria are met:

Criterion A – Function-limiting pain: I have had 12 months of progressive shoulder pain that is unrelieved by rest. I am currently unable to lift my arm above shoulder height and cannot sleep on the affected side. This directly documents loss of shoulder function interfering with activities of daily living.

Criterion B.1 – Failure to respond to at least three months of non-surgical management: I completed a supervised physical therapy program focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics for 16 weeks (2026-02-17 through 2026-06-09), totaling 24 visits, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. This exceeds the three-month non-surgical management requirement. In addition, I completed a 4-month trial of NSAIDs with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-07, which provided only 3 weeks of partial relief. This satisfies both the physical therapy/home exercise requirement and the medication/injection requirement of Criterion B.1.

Criterion C – Physical examination findings: My examination showed range of motion limited by pain, satisfying Criterion C.1.a (functionally limited active range of motion). My exam also documented positive provocative testing on the affected shoulder, satisfying Criterion C.2, which requires one or more positive orthopedic tests/signs. [Name(s) of the specific positive orthopedic test(s) performed, as documented in the exam note (e.g., Drop Arm Test, Painful Arc Test, Neer Impingement Test, Hawkins-Kennedy Impingement, etc.), should be confirmed from the full examination note and cited here.]

Criterion D – Advanced diagnostic imaging: MRI of the shoulder performed 2026-05-29 demonstrated a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm with grade 2 fatty atrophy. This finding is a full-thickness rotator cuff tear that correlates directly with my reported symptoms (inability to lift the arm above shoulder height, inability to sleep on the affected side) and with my physical examination findings (limited range of motion and positive provocative testing).

I have no active infection and no untreated substance use disorder that would contraindicate surgery. My BMI is 29, and I am a non-smoker. My treating surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, orthopedic surgery, has recommended rotator cuff repair based on this clinical picture.

Based on the above, my clinical record meets all four criteria (A through D) of PacificSource Medical Policy No. SUR228, "Shoulder Surgeries," for rotator cuff repair to be considered medically necessary. I respectfully request that PacificSource reverse the denial and authorize CPT 29827.

I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day window stated in the denial notice, with a deadline of 2027-02-02.

Enclosed/attached in support of this appeal:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-02-17 to 2026-06-09, 24 visits)
- Medication and injection records (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection 2026-05-07)
- MRI report dated 2026-05-29
- Physical examination note documenting range-of-motion limitation and positive orthopedic test findings
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Marchetti, orthopedic surgery
- [Any additional records the provider's office includes]

Please note: I have quoted directly from PacificSource Medical Policy No. SUR228, "Shoulder Surgeries," only the language I was able to obtain from that document. If PacificSource applied a different or updated version of this policy, or additional criteria not reproduced above, to my specific plan and date of service, I request that PacificSource identify and provide that exact policy language as part of this appeal review.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide written notice of the outcome, including the specific criteria applied, within the timeframe required for member appeals under my plan.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter. Please contact me at [phone number] or [email address] if additional information is needed.

Sincerely,

Emerson Delgado
